sentences.text: 2. M.Cr.C. No.3382/2024 is the second bail application on behalf of applicant Vijay Khushlani.
His first application bearing M.Cr.C. No.1938/2024 was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 01.04.2024 with liberty to repeat after filing of charge sheet.
3. M.Cr.C. No.3622/2024 is the first bail application on behalf of applicant Dileep Kumar Khuslani.
4. Both the above named applicants

are in custody in connection with Crime No.850/2023 registered at Police Station Thana City Kotwali, Raigarh District Raigarh(CG), for the offence punishable under Section 420, 467, 468, 471, 34 of the Indian Penal Code.

5. Case of prosecution, in brief, is that the complainant lodged written report in the concerned police-station alleging that applicant Vijay Khushlani is running a ready-made garments shop 'The Store'.
In course of business, time to time, he purchased ready-made clothes/garments from the complainant on credit, which accumulated to Rs.40,00,062/-.

When the demand is made, applicant Vijay Khushlani executed one mortgage deed in his favor, mortgaging one house in which a condition was imposed that he will not mortgage the same to any other person.
However, applicant Vijay Khushlani mortgaged the said house to one Ramesh Sachdeva in lieu of loan of Rs.10,00,000/- obtained by the said person and thereby he has committed the offence of cheating.
Based on the report initially FIR was registered under Section 420 of IPC and after completion of investigation, other offences were also added and applicants were arrested on 28.2.2024.
6. Learned counsel for applicants jointly submits that applicants are innocent persons and they have been falsely implicated in the crime in question.
They have not committed any offence as alleged.
Allegation against applicant Vijay Khushlani is that he purchased ready-made garments from the complainant on credit to the tune of Rs.40,00,062/-, but did not pay the said amount.

Allegation is purely of civil nature and, however, only to give it color of criminality, false allegation is levelled that applicant Vijay Khushlani has mortgaged the house to one Ramesh Sachdeva regarding which he has already executed a mortgage deed in favour of complainant.
7. Mr. Priyank Rathi, learned counsel for applicant in MCRC No.3622 of 2024 submits that the allegation of purchasing ready- made garments on credit is against Vijay Khushlani.

He was earlier granted bail by the learned Magistrate, however, after filing of the charge-sheet and adding of other offences under Sections 467, 468 & 471 of IPC when he moved application under Section 437 of IPC,
the same came to be rejected and he was arrested.
He also submits that the allegation or lodging of the report is only on account of non-payment of amount which was towards purchase of ready-made garments on credit.
Applicants are in jail since 28.2.2024, charge-sheet has been filed, hence, they may be enlarged on regular bail.
8. Per contra, learned State counsel opposes the submissions made by counsel for applicants.
However he does not dispute the submission made by counsel for applicants that charge-sheet has been filed.

9. Mr. Manoj Paranjpe and Mr. Hussain, learned counsel for complainant adopts the arguments made by counsel for the State and submit that not only applicant Vijay Khushlani has purchased the Vijay Khushlani vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 15 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47774222/

sentences.text: 2 clothes on credit with an assurance to repay the amount, but he has also not repaid the same.
Further the house which was mortgaged to the complainant was again mortgaged to some other person also and thereby they have committed the offence.
10. I have heard learned counsel for both the parties.

11. Taking into consideration facts and circumstances of the case, nature of allegations and also the submission of counsel for State that there is no criminal antecedent against applicants, without commenting anything on merits of case, I feel inclined to allow bail application of applicants.

12. Accordingly, bail applications are allowed and it is directed that applicant Vijay Khushlani in M.Cr.C. No.3382/2024 and applicant Dileep Kumar Khuslani in M.Cr.C. No.3622/2024, shall be released on bail on their furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.25,000/- each with one surety in the like sum to the satisfaction of trial Court concerned on the conditions that;  they shall appear before the trial Court concerned regularly on each & every date unless exempted from appearance. 
they shall not, in any manner, tamper with the prosecution witnesses.
If they are found involved in similar offence in future, it will be open for the State to apply for cancellation of bail.
